subject.title: feat(compaction): add identifier survival validation after summarization

question: Should this PR land with strict compaction cancelling when post-cap identifier recovery cannot fit, once runtime proof is supplied, or should that fail-closed behavior be narrowed or split?
rationale: The code now fixes a real session-state/security bug, but strict cancellation is an intentional upgrade-sensitive behavior change that source review alone should not silently accept for existing users.

options.title: Require proof, then accept strict cancel
options.body: Ask for redacted runtime compaction proof at the current head and land the PR if the proof shows the fail-closed path behaves as intended.

options.title: Narrow to sanitizer first
options.body: Land only the credential-sanitization fix first and keep strict post-cap cancellation for a smaller follow-up after live-session proof.

options.title: Accept source-level proof only
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the helper-script and unit-test evidence, but they own the remaining live-session uncertainty.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then accept strict cancel
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted runtime compaction proof at the current head and land the PR if the proof shows the fail-closed path behaves as intended.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR author explicitly requested steipete's review and git history shows recent adjacent compaction planning work in this area.
